svg.text: Essence: A skill is a folder of instructions, scripts, and assets that an agent loads on demand. Skills give a
simple general-purpose agent the domain expertise, repeatable workflows, and new capabilities it lacks — and
they are now an open standard, so one skill works across many different AI products.
• A skill is a lightweight, open format for extending what an AI agent can do.
• A skill is a folder of organized files: a SKILL.md file plus subfolders that hold instructions,
scripts, images, and other resources it can reference.
• The SKILL.md is not just text — it can point to scripts and say when to run them (for
example, a PDF skill that converts pages to images or fills form fields).
🤖 Why Skills? From single-purpose agents to one general agent
We used to build a separate agent for each job — coding, research, finance, marketing — each with
its own tools and context. But under the hood they all need the same thing: a simple scaffolding.
New idea: one general-purpose agent — code is the universal interface
• Simple scaffolding: just bash and a filesystem — easy to test, scale, understand.
• But it still needs context and domain expertise to do the job reliably.
• Skills fill that gap — and travel with the agent across ecosystems.
🎯 What Skills give an agent (loaded on demand)
Skills provide procedural knowledge and company-, team-, and user-specific context. Three kinds:
Do a task your way: brand guidelines and templates, legal review
Predictable steps in a non-deterministic system: weekly marketing
campaign review, customer call prep, quarterly business review.
Things it could not do before: create presentations, generate Excel
sheets or PDF reports, build MCP servers, run scripts when needed.
• You had to describe your instructions and requirements every time.
• You had to bundle all references and supporting files into context every time.
• You had to work hard to keep the workflow and outputs consistent across people and runs.
Because Skills are an open standard, one skill runs unchanged in Claude Code, Claude.ai, the
Claude Agent SDK and API — and in a growing list of other agent products. Build once, share, scale.
Combine custom and built-in skills into one complex, predictable workflow. Each box below is one
skill; the agent chains them left to right:
You can have hundreds of skills. To protect the context window, a skill is loaded in three stages —
only what is needed enters context. The context window is a public good: fewer tokens = clearer answers.
1 · Metadata — the skill's name and description.
Always loaded so the agent knows the skill exists and when to trigger it (~30–50 tokens each).
Loaded only when the skill is triggered — the full steps enter context at that moment, not before.
3 · Resources — extra reference files and scripts.
Loaded only as needed. Scripts run through bash separately, so their code never pollutes the
context window — the agent adds only what is truly necessary.
Result: Claude uses bash + a filesystem to read files and run scripts on demand, keeping the
context small while still reaching a large library of skills.
• On Dec 18, 2025, Anthropic published the Agent Skills specification as a public open standard:
a folder + a SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter) + the three-tier progressive-disclosure design.
• By early March 2026 (~12 weeks later), OpenAI Codex, Microsoft, JetBrains, Cursor, Gemini CLI,
Block's Goose and 25+ other agent products had shipped compatible implementations.
• A skill you build for Claude runs identically in those tools — one format, 20+ platforms.
Sources listed in the chat reply.
Skills turn a simple, general agent into a reliable expert without bloating it. Package the how
once — instructions, scripts, assets — and progressive disclosure loads it only when relevant. The
agent stays portable, composable, and cheap on context while gaining deep, repeatable skill.
